metadata.chunk_title: What questions will the admission application ask?

facts.value: Self-reporting is recommended because it will greatly speed up the time it takes to receive an admission decision.

metadata.chunk_title: What questions will the admission application ask?

facts.value: If you are unable or choose not to self-report your grades, you can have your school submit your official transcripts to ASU.

metadata.chunk_title: What questions will the admission application ask?

facts.value: If you know what you want to study, visit ASU’s degree page to see if it’s offered. If you are still figuring out what you want to major in, that’s normal too. Try one of ASU’s exploratory programs, which enable you to explore different academic areas without losing any time or credit toward your degree. You can also take ASU’s major and career quiz, me3®, which can help you narrow down the right major for you. Additionally, try talking to your academic advisor for guidance. And know that you’re not alone — 80 percent of students switch majors at least once.

metadata.chunk_title: How do I pick a major?

facts.value: Grades are considered in the admission process, with some programs requiring higher grades than the university average. Good grades are important for admission to Barrett, The Honors College, although there is no minimum GPA requirement.

metadata.chunk_title: How important are grades in admission? + How many colleges should I apply to? + When should I take the SAT or ACT?

facts.value: There is no specific number of colleges to apply to; it varies by student. It is recommended to apply to more than one college for options if not admitted to the preferred college.

metadata.chunk_title: How important are grades in admission? + How many colleges should I apply to? + When should I take the SAT or ACT?

facts.value: Most students take the ACT or SAT in the spring of their junior year, summer after junior year, or fall of their senior year. It is also suggested to take the PSAT in October of junior year for consideration in National Merit and National Recognition Scholarship programs.
